---
This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game). Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.
"

22: - Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable pixel-art arcade fighting game inspired by Mortal Kombat and Street Fighter.
- Add the requested fighting controls: weak/medium/strong punches and kicks, jump, block, grapple, special move, and finishing move.

## Requirements
- Playable game; no clarifying questions.
- User’s latest control requirements are still unimplemented.

## Decisions
- Built an original game branded “RIFT//CLASH” with original fighters and visuals rather than using copyrighted characters.

## Work State
### Completed
- Created `index.html` with a responsive pixel-art fighting game, CPU opponent, rounds, health and energy meters, sound toggle, and touch controls.
- JavaScript syntax checked successfully before the user’s latest request.

### Active
- Expand gameplay and controls to implement six attack strengths/types, jump, block, grapple, special, and finishing move.
- Update desktop and touch control hints/buttons to match implemented actions.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect and edit `index.html` to implement the requested control set and gameplay mechanics.
2. Update the HUD/tutorial and mobile touch controls, then syntax-check and test the game.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Entire game implementation and interface.

## Important Context
- Current controls are A/D movement, W jump, J punch, K kick, L chi blast, S block; mobile buttons offer movement, jump, chi, kick, and hit.
- Grapple, multiple attack strengths, and finishing move are not currently implemented.
- Changes are uncommitted.

## Objective
- Complete the RIFT//CLASH fighting game with the requested combat controls, updated HUD/tutorial, and mobile touch controls.

## Requirements
- Implement weak/medium/strong punches and kicks, jump, block, grapple, special move, and finishing move.
- Update the HUD/tutorial and mobile controls, then syntax-check and test the game.

## Decisions
- Desktop controls: A/D to move; W to jump; J/U/I for punches; K/O/P for kicks; S to block; G to grapple; L for special; F for finisher.
- Finisher requires full energy and CPU health at or below 25%.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added six attack strengths/types, grapple, special projectile, and finisher mechanics in `index.html`.
- Updated the title tutorial, HUD finisher hint, and mobile touch buttons.
- Extracted the game script and ran `node --check /tmp/opencode/rift-clash.js` successfully.

### Active
- Test the game in-browser, including the desktop and touch controls and the finisher unlock/activation.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Run the game in a browser and verify combat, controls, HUD, and responsive touch controls.
2. Fix any issues revealed by gameplay testing.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Contains the complete game, controls, mechanics, and interface.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- Syntax was checked; gameplay/browser testing has not yet been performed.

## Objective
- Expand RIFT//CLASH with a visible, playable character roster from Mortal Kombat and Street Fighter.
- Add character selection and show selected fighter names in the title screen and HUD.

## Requirements
- Include 15 randomly selected characters drawn from both franchises.
- Provide selectable fighter choices and a character-select experience.

## Decisions
- Use a title-screen selection flow rather than a separate screen: Q/E cycles the player, A/D cycles the CPU; Enter starts the fight.
- Show selected names on the title screen and above each fighter’s HUD.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added two 15-character source rosters and a randomized `featuredRoster` of 15.
- Added title-screen player/CPU selection indicators and selection key handling.
- Added fighter names to fighter state and the in-game HUD.

### Active
- Validate and fix the character-selection implementation; syntax-check and test gameplay and selection.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect `index.html` for integration issues, especially selection updates, touch behavior, and round resets.
2. Extract the script and run `node --check`.
3. Test title selection, starting/rematching, and fighter names in the HUD; fix any issues found.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game code, roster data, selection flow, title screen, and HUD.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- Earlier combat mechanics and controls were implemented; script syntax passed before the latest character-selection edits, which have not yet been checked.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Expand RIFT//CLASH with 15 selectable Mortal Kombat and Street Fighter characters, show their names in the title screen and HUD, and add more visual detail to the fighters.

## Requirements
- Include 15 randomly selected characters drawn from both franchises.
- Make fighter choices selectable and visible to players.

## Decisions
- Use title-screen selection: Q/E cycles the player, A/D cycles the CPU; Enter starts the fight.
- Show selected fighter names on the title screen and above each fighter’s HUD.
- Add distinct appearance details for each character.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added a randomized 15-character roster split between Mortal Kombat and Street Fighter.
- Added keyboard title-screen selection, visible selected names, and fighter names in the HUD.
- Added pointer-based selection on the title canvas.

### Active
- Integrate the newly added per-character appearance data into fighter rendering so the fighters look distinct.
- Validate selection, gameplay, round resets, and script syntax.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect `index.html` and connect `characterLooks` to `drawFighter`; the existing renderer still uses generic palettes.
2. Extract the inline script and run `node --check`.
3. Test character selection, starting/rematching, and name/appearance updates in the HUD and gameplay.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game code, roster, character selection, per-character appearance data, renderer, and HUD.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- `characterLooks` was added with distinct color and feature data for all 30 roster characters, but is not yet used by `drawFighter`.
- The mobile title-screen pointer selection chooses fighters by tapping the left/right canvas areas; touch-control buttons no longer auto-start the fight.

from pathlib import Path
import re
html=Path('index.html').read_text()
scripts=re.findall(r'<script>(.*?)</script>', html, re.S)
assert len(scripts)==1, f'expected one inline script, got {len(scripts)}'
Path('/tmp/opencode/rift-clash.js').write_text(scripts[0])
PY
node --check /tmp/opencode/rift-clash.js

python3 - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
import re
s=Path('index.html').read_text()
looks=set(re.findall(r"^\s*'([^']+)':makeLook",s,re.M))
rosters=set(re.findall(r"const (?:mkRoster|sfRoster)=\[([^\]]+)\]",s))
roster_names=set(re.findall(r"'([^']+)'",' '.join(rosters)))
print(f'character looks: {len(looks)}; roster entries: {len(roster_names)}; missing looks: {sorted(roster_names-looks)}')
PY

1: ## Process lifecycle
2: 
3: - Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
4: - Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
5: - After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.
6: 
7: ## Linux browser and WebGPU capture
8: 
9: - Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
10: - Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
11: - Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
12: - Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
13: - Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
14: - Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
15: - Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
16: - Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
17: - Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.
18: 
19: ## Mobile browser games
20: 
21: - Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
22: - Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
23: - Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
24: - Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.
